title: Christmas Comes Early For The US Consumer
text:
Christmas Comes Early For The US Consumer

Tan Kai Xian

Gavekal Research | 10 Nov 2026

Despite the recent convulsions in the US equity market, things are looking up for the ordinary US consumer, and for US consumer stocks. For much of the post-Covid period, the US economy was described as “K-shaped.” Untroubled by moderating income growth, asset-rich households continued to spend, encouraged by the rising value of their equity portfolios. In contrast, asset-poor consumers found themselves squeezed by a soft labor market, higher energy prices and inflation, and higher borrowing costs. For significant segments of the market, Donald Trump’s strict immigration policies compounded the effects of this squeeze, as consumer businesses serving immigrant communities saw their client bases shrink.Now, things are turning around. The labor market has tightened. And the Democratic Party’s gains in last Tuesday’s midterm elections point to cheaper pump prices for gasoline and diesel, as well as a less severe stance on immigration. There remain sizable risks, including the possibility that the US AI capex engine could stall. Nevertheless, the headwinds that have held back a large portion of the US consumer market now appear to be fading.
